wave_orbit_title: One orbit produces two wave cycles
wave_detector_desc: A laser reaches a beam splitter and travels along two perpendicular arms. The wave changes the two arm lengths oppositely. Mirrors move by a magnified amount in this diagram; readouts show the physical length difference.
wave_curve_title: Two signal cycles during one orbit
wave_null: Detector is blind to this plus component
wave_x_longer: X arm longer · Y arm shorter
wave_y_longer: Y arm longer · X arm shorter
wave_balanced: Arms have equal length at this moment
wave_intro: Follow one orbit of two black holes. Two wave cycles pass the detector during that orbit, alternately lengthening and shortening its arms. These three views show the same selected moment.
wave_orbit_note: The cross marks the center of mass. Orbit and horizon sizes share a scale that fits this view; colored locator rings help you find small black holes.
wave_detector_note: Solid arms show magnified motion; gray dotted lines mark their resting lengths. Each real arm is 4 km. The physical length difference appears below.
wave_scale_note: Vertical scale adjusts to fit the wave. One chart unit equals
wave_scale_compare: Compare readouts when changing sources or distance.
wave_scrub_help: Drag the chart, or focus it and use arrow keys. Home selects the start; End completes one orbit.
wave_null_key: At 45°, this detector has no response to the plus component even though the wave is present.
wave_gain_limits: Magnification adjusts to the arriving wave; it does not change the physical readouts.
wave_playback_note: Playback takes about 10 seconds per orbit. Physical time follows the selected frequency. Playback stops at the end, and controls pause it.
wave_controls_note: Masses are measured at the source. Redshift stretches the arriving signal’s time scale. Distance and redshift can be chosen independently here; the controls do not fit a cosmological model.
wave_frequency_limit_note: Frequency is capped for an early orbit with relative orbital speed at most 0.3 times light speed:
wave_frequency_clamp: Changing mass or redshift can lower this limit.
wave_orientation_label: X arm angle to plus axis
wave_reference_values: The initial 2016 discovery paper estimated source masses of 36 and 29 Suns, luminosity distance 410 Mpc, and redshift 0.09. This model uses those rounded estimates; the wave frequency and ideal viewing geometry are chosen.
wave_custom_values: These source settings are a teaching example. Restore GW150914 inputs to use the initial published mass, distance, and redshift estimates.
wave_observation_limits: The observed event swept upward in frequency through inspiral, merger, and ringdown. This view holds one early orbit at a fixed frequency. It does not reproduce the recorded strain or the merger.
wave_model_law: A circular orbit uses Newtonian gravity, and a leading quadrupole formula sets the wave amplitude. The ideal source is face-on. The plus component travels perpendicular to the detector plane. Each arm changes by ±Lh/2; their difference is Lh, with L = 4,000 m.
wave_model_limits: The detector reads only the plus component here. Real waves also have a cross component, and real detectors use optical cavities, feedback, and noise filtering. Spins, full inspiral evolution, merger physics, travel delays, and measurement noise are omitted. This is not a detector sensitivity forecast.
